title: SEVERE WEATHER
full_story:
Clay County experienced severe weather again last night and early this morning.

At around 7 pm the National Weather Service office issued a tornado warning for northern Clay County.  The Weather Service said they had radar indicated rotation near Edgewood and Mason.  At 7:05 they indicated that doppler radar had picked up a tornado near Edgewood.  Steve Lewis with Clay County ESDA reported their were some medium sized tree limbs down, but didn’t report any other damage.  Clay Electric COOP dispatched linemen last night to repair power outages north of Louisville.  Rain amounts varied with in the storm between .5” to just over 1” measured early this morning.

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY
full_story:
Friday afternoon the Flora Police Department, alongside Clay County Sheriff’s Office conducted an “Intruder Alert” training exercise at the Flora High School.

The exercise began after students had been dismissed for the weekend.  As a result, there was an increased presence of squad cars and personnel at the school.

While it is exceedingly rare for any specific school to be the victim of an armed attack, the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE) mandates an Intruder Drill be held within the first three months of each school year.

Then on Thursday, at approximately 7:36 pm, an officer with the Flora Police Department initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle traveling on US Highway 50 between North State Road and North Olive Road.

During the course of the traffic stop, the driver was asked to exit the vehicle but refused.  Flora Police Department officers eventually removed the driver from the vehicle. Clay County Sheriff’s Deputies arrived on scene to assist officers.

A subsequent search warrant was conducted on a residence in Clay City by the Clay County Sheriff’s Office and the Flora Police Department.

As a result of this incident, Joshua R. Sullens, 43, of Clay City, was arrested for the following offenses; Resisting or Obstructing a Peace Officer; Aggravated Assault; Possession of Methamphetamine (100–400 grams); Methamphetamine Delivery; Possession of Cannabis (100–500 grams); Possession with the intent to Deliver Cannabis (500 grams-2,000 grams); and Possession of Drug Paraphernalia.

The Flora Police Department and Clay County Sheriff’s Office continue their investigation and will provide additional information if necessary as it becomes available and can be released.

The Flora Police Department was also assisted in the investigation by the Clay County State Attorney’s Office.

All charges are allegations, and Sullens is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: PAINTOUT 26
full_story:
The 2026 Fairfield PaintOut will welcome 25 talented artists to Fairfield for its 15th annual event starting tomorrow.

On Tuesday, artists may paint anywhere before settling in with their host families.  Orientation will be held at 5 pm at Fusion Coffee Shop.

On Wednesday, artists may paint anywhere in Wayne County before gathering that evening at the home of committee members Keith and Dena Stout for a meal and fellowship.  They will also have the opportunity to participate in a nocturne paint.

Thursday will include an optional trip to Cedarhurst Museum in Mount Vernon, where artists are invited to paint for the Spencer Meagher Legacy category.  The museum will be open from 10 am to 5 pm, and lunch will be provided for artists making the trip.  Artists may also choose to paint elsewhere in Wayne County.

On Friday, artists may continue painting anywhere in Wayne County but must turn in all paintings at Fairfield CP Church by 3:30 pm for the Art Show and Sale.

Saturday’s activities will feature a Youth Chalk Art Show in the CP Church parking lot.  Artist judging will continue until 11 am, with awards announced at noon.

Community members are encouraged to watch for artists working throughout the area during PaintOut week.  The Fairfield PaintOut Facebook page has also been featuring individual artist biographies leading up to and during the event, giving the public an opportunity to learn more about the artists and their work.

The week will culminate with the PaintOut Art Show and Sale, offering the public an opportunity to view and purchase artwork created during this year’s event.

title: DRIVE THRU FLU SHOT CLINIC
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is sponsoring a number of drive thru Flu shot clinics.  The next will be Wednesday from 9 am until 4 pm at the Health Department.  People wanting flu shots should follow the signs to the carport, no appointment is needed.  Please bring your Medicare Part B Card, HMO Card, Medicaid Card, or insurance card.  If uninsured, underinsured, or insurance is out of network, you may be charged a small administration fee.

There will also be drive through clinics on September 30th, October 7th, October 14th, October 21st and October 28th at the Health Department, from 9 to 4.

The Health Department will also be administering flu shots at the Xenia Community Center on October 7th from 11:30 to 12:30, at the Ingraham Bank on October 8th from 9 to 10 am, at the Louisville Farm Bureau October 13th from 10:15 to 11:15, at the Clay City Bank on October 16th from 9 to 10 am.

The Health Department says getting the flu vaccine is the best way to protect yourself, your family, and your community from the flu.  The Health Department will be administering the trivalent flu vaccine or the higher dose influenza vaccinations.  Different flu strains circulate every flu season, making it important that you get an annual flu shot.

title: ISP URGES HOMECOMING SAFETY
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) reminds teens and their families to enjoy homecoming celebrations responsibly this year because the choices made today can have lasting consequences.

In July 2026, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) published its Young Driver Traffic Safety Fact Sheet, which showed young people between the ages of 15 and 20 years old, accounted for 9% of all drivers involved in a fatal traffic crash.  The Fact Sheet also showed 53% of young drivers killed were not wearing a seatbelt and 29% had alcohol in their system.  In Illinois, the leading contributing causes of major injury and fatal crashes are commonly referred to as “fatal four” violations; impaired driving, speeding, distracted driving, and improper seatbelt usage.

“ISP is doing its part to help prevent tragedies this homecoming season through increased traffic enforcement and patrols, but also through safety education,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.  “We encourage parents and guardians to discuss the dangers of alcohol and drug use with their children, including not getting in a car with a driver who has been consuming drugs or alcohol.”

Illinois is a zero-tolerance state when it comes to underage drinking, it is illegal for any person under the age of 21 to possess or consume any amount of an alcoholic beverage.  Violators may be cited, fined, or arrested, and vehicles will be towed.

In addition to staying sober, young drivers should follow the speed limit, wear their seatbelts, even in the backseat, and avoid phone use and other distractions while driving.  Illinois law prohibits cellphone usage for young drivers under age 19, including a hands-free device, except to call law enforcement or emergency services.

The ISP Safety Education Unit offers a wide variety of free educational programs for schools and community groups throughout Illinois.  For more information on the programs offered, visit https://isp.illinois.gov/TrafficSafety/SafetyEducation or email [email protected].

Cheer for your team and have fun at the big dance, but do so responsibly and get home safely.

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 am from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: ILLINOIS UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) announced that the unemployment rate was 4.7 percent in August, down -0.2 percentage point from July, and up +0.4 percentage point from the same month, one year ago, based on data provided by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).  The revised July unemployment rate was 4.9 percent.

Total nonfarm payrolls decreased over-the-month in August, down 4,400 to 6,175,600.  The July monthly change in payrolls was revised from the preliminary report, from up 11,700 to up 15,300.  The August payroll jobs estimate and unemployment rate reflect activity for the week including the 12th.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases included: Leisure and Hospitality up 1,800, Construction up 1,500, and Professional and Business Services up 1,000.  The sectors with the largest over-the-month jobs decreases included: Private Education and Health Services down 6,100, Financial Activities down 1,700, and Trade, Transportation and Utilities down 1,000.

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were up 15,000 jobs.  The industry groups with the largest jobs increases included: Construction up 13,400, Private Education and Health Services up 9,600, and Other Services up 4,000.  The industry groups with the largest jobs decreases included: Financial Activities down 15,800, Information down 2,900 and Trade, Transportation and Utilities down 700.  In August, total nonfarm payrolls were up 0.2% over-the-year in Illinois and up 0.4% in the nation.

title: ISP HARVEST SAFETY
full_story:
Illinois State Police troopers are urging drivers and farmers to share the road this fall harvest season.

Troopers warn that the coming months will bring an influx of slow-moving machinery traveling between fields on public roads. Illinois Department of Transportation data recorded 275 crashes involving farm tractors or equipment statewide in 2024.

State police advise drivers to reduce speeds, increase following distance behind wide machinery, and watch for amber flashing lights and slow-moving vehicle emblems. Passing is prohibited in no-passing zones and within 100 feet of intersections, railroad crossings, and bridges. Drivers should also watch for hand signals from farmers driving older equipment without turn indicators.

Authorities also ask farmers to avoid traveling during peak traffic hours, bad weather, or after dark when possible. Operators should ensure all lights and reflectors are clear of dust and field debris, and safely pull onto shoulders when feasible to allow backed-up traffic to pass.
